title: Proxmox cluster
description: Is the Proxmox cluster healthy? Quorum, nodes, guests that should run, where the load sits, storage and thin-pool headroom, backup coverage. Open it after a Pve*, ThinPool* or PveStorageFilling alert, or on the weekly review.

panels.title: Cluster quorum
panels.description: Proxmox cluster quorum (rule PveClusterNotQuorate). Three nodes: one down keeps quorum, two down lose it. Not quorate means guests keep running but start, stop, config changes and backups lock. DOWN also shows when the exporter has no cluster series at all. Whole cluster; the Node selector does not filter this tile.

panels.title: Nodes down
panels.description: Nodes the cluster sees offline (rule PveNodeDown, 2 minutes). Red at 1 or more. The alert's severity follows the node's tier: pve2 and pve3 critical, pve1 warning, because it is always on since ADR 0023. Whole cluster, not filtered by the Node selector.

panels.title: Guests down
panels.description: Guests with onboot=1 that are not running (rule PveGuestDown: 5 minutes). The archive CT and the `ai` VM have onboot=0 and are stopped by design, so they never count here; the guest table below shows them as 'stopped'.

targets.expr: count((pve_up{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"} == 0) * on (id) group_left (name, node) pve_guest_info and on (id) (pve_onboot_status == 1))

panels.title: Guests not backed up
panels.description: Guests in no backup job (rule PveGuestNotBackedUp, 1 hour; the PBS CT is excluded on purpose). It counts coverage only: there is no backup success or age metric yet, so a green tile does not prove the last backup worked. A freshness collector is planned and will add panels here.

targets.expr: count((pve_not_backed_up_info == 1) * on (id) group_left (name, node) pve_guest_info{template="0"} unless on (id) pve_guest_info{name="pbs"})

panels.title: Thin pool data, fullest
panels.description: Data allocated in the fullest guest thin pool (pve/data, one per node). Orange above 85 % (rule ThinPoolFilling), red above 92 % (ThinPoolCritical). The pool auto-extends at 80 % into a small buffer; at 100 % every guest on it freezes. Whole cluster.

panels.title: Thin pool metadata, fullest
panels.description: Metadata used in the fullest thin pool. Orange above 75 % (rule ThinPoolMetadataFilling). Full metadata stops the pool like full data does; the fix is lvextend --poolmetadatasize. Whole cluster.

panels.title: Storage fullest
panels.description: The fullest directory or PBS storage (rule PveStorageFilling: over 90 % for 30 minutes, warning). Thin pools are not in it (tiles to the left). Today the PBS datastore is the one to watch; the runway panel below turns this into days.

panels.title: Node memory, fullest
panels.description: Memory in use on the fullest Proxmox node, 1 minus MemAvailable/MemTotal (rule HostMemoryLow fires below 10 % available for 15 minutes, which is 90 % here). The k3s VMs fall under the same rule but are not shown on this board.

panels.title: Is every guest that should run, running?
Guests
panels.description: Every guest on the selected nodes: where it runs, whether it is running, whether it starts on boot, and CPU and memory against its own limit. Stopped guests sort first. A stopped guest with On boot = yes is what rule PveGuestDown alerts on; stopped with On boot = no (archive, ai) is by design. CPU is the share of the guest's own vCPUs. A VM's memory can read slightly above 100 % (k3s does at the time of writing): Proxmox reports what the host sees the VM using, and the number is not clamped here.

targets.expr: max by (id, name, node, type) ((pve_up{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"}) * on (id) group_left (name, node, type) pve_guest_info{node=~"$node"})
max by (id, name, node, type) ((max by (id) (pve_onboot_status)) * on (id) group_left (name, node, type) pve_guest_info{node=~"$node"})
max by (id, name, node, type) ((pve_cpu_usage_limit{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"}) * on (id) group_left (name, node, type) pve_guest_info{node=~"$node"})
max by (id, name, node, type) ((pve_cpu_usage_ratio{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"}) * on (id) group_left (name, node, type) pve_guest_info{node=~"$node"})
max by (id, name, node, type) ((pve_memory_usage_bytes{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"}) * on (id) group_left (name, node, type) pve_guest_info{node=~"$node"})
max by (id, name, node, type) ((pve_memory_size_bytes{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"}) * on (id) group_left (name, node, type) pve_guest_info{node=~"$node"})
max by (id, name, node, type) ((pve_memory_usage_bytes{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"} / pve_memory_size_bytes{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"}) * on (id) group_left (name, node, type) pve_guest_info{node=~"$node"})

panels.title: Guests that start on boot
panels.description: Up (green) and down (red) per guest that should always run (onboot=1), over the dashboard's time range. A red bar is what rule PveGuestDown measures; a node reboot shows as a short red bar on every guest it hosts. The `ai` VM and the archive CT are not listed: they are off by design.

panels.title: Nodes and quorum
panels.description: Each node's state as the cluster sees it (rule PveNodeDown) and quorum (rule PveClusterNotQuorate) over time. Two nodes red at once, with quorum red, is the dangerous case. HA is not in use here: no HA resources exist, so every pve_ha_state series reads 0.

panels.title: CPU used by guest, in cores
panels.description: CPU each guest uses, as cores: its CPU ratio times its vCPU count, so guests of different sizes compare directly. The legend shows the mean and the peak over the range. Utilisation, not an alert: a guest pinned at its vCPU count is starved (see the vCPUs column in the table); a node's total is below.

panels.title: Node CPU
panels.description: CPU utilisation of each Proxmox node, share of all its cores. No alert watches CPU load (HostCpuHot is temperature, on the Hardware board). Sustained 90 % or more means a guest needs moving or limiting.

panels.title: Memory used by guest
panels.description: Memory each guest uses, as Proxmox reports it. Compare with the Memory limit column in the guest table: a guest near its limit is killed by the kernel (CT) or swaps (VM). A VM can read slightly above its configured size.

panels.title: Node memory used
panels.description: Memory in use per Proxmox node, 1 minus MemAvailable/MemTotal. The dashed line is the 90 % that rule HostMemoryLow fires at (10 % available for 15 minutes). pve3 has the least RAM, so it is the first to run out.

panels.title: Memory committed vs node memory
panels.description: Memory promised to guests as a share of each node's RAM: 'configured' counts every guest placed on the node, 'running' only those up now. Over 100 % (orange) means the guests could together claim more than the node has. No alert mirrors this. pve1's configured bar includes the 24 GiB `ai` VM, so it reads far above its running bar while the VM is off.

targets.expr: sum by (node) (pve_memory_size_bytes{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"} * on (id) group_left (node) pve_guest_info) / on (node) label_replace(pve_memory_size_bytes{id=~"node/.*"}, "node", "$1", "id", "node/(.*)")

sum by (node) (pve_memory_size_bytes{id=~"(lxc|qemu)/.*"} * on (id) group_left (node) (pve_guest_info and on (id) (pve_up == 1))) / on (node) label_replace(pve_memory_size_bytes{id=~"node/.*"}, "node", "$1", "id", "node/(.*)")

panels.title: Network by guest
panels.description: Bytes per second in plus out on each guest's virtual NIC. Shows which guest moves the data. A step change with no deploy behind it is worth a look.

panels.title: Disk I/O by guest
panels.description: Bytes per second read plus written on each guest's disks. The thin pool and the SSDs are shared, so one guest writing hard slows the rest. Sustained high writes from a stateful guest (monitoring, postgres, the k3s VMs) also wear the SSD.

panels.title: Storage used
panels.description: How full each directory and PBS storage is. Orange from 90 % (rule PveStorageFilling, 30 minutes). `pbs` is the nightly backup datastore (it lives on the PBS CT's own disk) and `pbs-replica` its off-node copy; both are shared storages, so each shows once. The thin pools (local-lvm) are on the next panels.

targets.expr: max by (storage) ((pve_disk_usage_bytes{id=~"storage/.*"} / pve_disk_size_bytes{id=~"storage/.*"}) * on (id) group_left (storage) pve_storage_info{plugintype="pbs"})

panels.title: Storage used over time
panels.description: The same ratios over time, with the 90 % alert line (rule PveStorageFilling) dashed. A steady climb towards the line is the thing to plan for; a flat line is fine at any height. `local` is the fullest of the three nodes' root storages.

targets.expr: max by (storage) ((pve_disk_usage_bytes{id=~"storage/.*"} / pve_disk_size_bytes{id=~"storage/.*"}) * on (id) group_left (storage) pve_storage_info{plugintype=~"pbs|dir"})

panels.title: Days until a storage reaches 90 %
panels.description: Days until each storage crosses the 90 % line of rule PveStorageFilling if the last 7 days of change continue (linear, capped at 365; flat or shrinking reads 365; already over the line reads 0). Under 30 days is worth a plan, under 7 is urgent. A freshly seeded copy like `pbs-replica` grows fast at first and reads low.

targets.expr: min by (storage) (clamp_max(clamp_min(0.9 * pve_disk_size_bytes{id=~"storage/.*", id!~"storage/.*/local-lvm"} - pve_disk_usage_bytes{id=~"storage/.*", id!~"storage/.*/local-lvm"}, 0) / clamp_min(deriv(pve_disk_usage_bytes{id=~"storage/.*", id!~"storage/.*/local-lvm"}[7d]), 1) / 86400, 365) * on (id) group_left (storage) pve_storage_info)

panels.title: Thin pool data allocated
panels.description: Data allocated in each node's guest thin pool (pve/data). Dashed lines are the alert thresholds: 85 % ThinPoolFilling, 92 % ThinPoolCritical. The pool auto-extends at 80 % into a small VG buffer, so sitting above 85 % means the buffer is being used up; at 100 % every guest on the pool freezes. pve3 has the smallest pool. Fix: pct fstrim in the guests, or add disk.

panels.title: Thin pool metadata used
panels.description: Metadata used in each thin pool. The dashed line is 75 % (rule ThinPoolMetadataFilling). Metadata grows with the number of snapshots and blocks, not with data; it is far from the line today and moves slowly.

panels.title: Guests in no backup job
panels.description: Guests that no backup job covers (rule PveGuestNotBackedUp: still listed after 1 hour it alerts). Empty is the goal. The nightly job (PBS, 02:30 WIB) covers every guest except the PBS CT itself, whose disk is the datastore, so a new guest is covered automatically; an entry here means the job was edited, disabled or removed, or the guest is one the rule does not exclude. This is coverage only: there is no backup success or age metric yet.

targets.expr: (pve_not_backed_up_info == 1) * on (id) group_left (name, node) pve_guest_info{template="0"} unless on (id) pve_guest_info{name="pbs"}

panels.title: Not measured yet
panels.description: Reading guide.

options.content: **Backup freshness is not on this board.** Proxmox exports whether a guest is in a backup job, not whether the last run succeeded or how old it is. A freshness collector is planned and will add panels here. Until then a failed nightly run reaches Telegram only as a Proxmox notification, and a restore is the real proof (`docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md`).
